user_intent: Audit and improve relationships, organized-crime operations/roles, rival TPP development, complete crossover/Noxian roster integration, and living-world causality across Season 3.
sources: Riot Universe Noxus region and Riot champion insights Samira
authority: Current author feedback and delivered matching-branch episodes supersede dated future labels; full source owners govern actual capabilities, personality, presence and source-world fidelity.

relationships.finding: Current delivered E30–31 mostly use reactive quips and functional tactical cooperation; the group rarely has its own changing family arguments, private tenderness, jealous pride, distrust, competing desired purchases, gifts, lingering embarrassment or a hard choice that alters a later bond. One resolved tactical disagreement in E31 (Daniel suggests sharing a chest; Arthur negotiates; Chris knows unpaid workers; Kaze authorizes) is a positive model.
relationships.existing_rule: Chosen family, no permanent commander, anyone can instigate/refuse, serious disloyalty is consequential, no compulsory cooperation, no equal scene attendance. Pairwise history and private motive live in Group_Relationships; do not treat every other Sin as Kaze's follower or flatten physical affection and hostility to one joke.
relationships.application: Trace at least one active *relationship consequence* when organically motivated: somebody's action changes whether another helps, trusts, owes, competes, imitates, protects or later resents them; carry that change forward. Do not install a numeric relationship quota or force antagonism.

outlaw_operations.confirmed_business_model: Self-directed organized-chaotic criminal chosen family: big scores, hired work by their choice, greed, pleasure, revenge, stolen goods, personal prizes and risk. Informal situational job leader, NOT Kaze permanent boss. Actual-job net-profit rule: leader earns 60 percent; remaining 40 percent split among OTHER participating Sins, distinguishing cost recovery/previous shares and independently owned valuables. Participation, overrides and custody require actual evidence.

Arthur: persuasive outlaw scheme/hostile negotiation, cyber-eye tactical surveillance, precision-to-artillery firepower, personal low-honor economics; neither sole strategist nor permanent restrained chaperone.
Chris: active chef/gunman, technical burglary/fabrication, fine precision, opportunistic scavenging, inventory disputes, intelligence from conversations; not only scavenger or weapon counter.

Billy: independent predator, transport/storage and custody through BELLY/Bayou, massive physical force, social hospitality/bargaining, appetite and ancient music/vanity; NOT a passive magical bank vault. Exterior body alternates with Chris under one-exterior rule.
Daniel: simian scout/mobility, versatile combat, drunk situational trickster, fast manipulation and genuine strategic/bargaining contributions; not just banter or Kaze's sidekick.

systemic_operating_failures: No sustained enterprise/score appetite between episodic roadblock encounters; crimes finish but seldom alter what the gang can afford, threaten, buy, ransom or celebrate.
Uncounted E31 two chests and E28 unallocated 2,100 plus older 20 silver are separate. No automatic division, spending, return-on-investment, new business or new asset grant.
BELLY's private storage, prisoners, security and inside details must stay private; witnessed swallowing can change witness knowledge without exposing internal floorplan.
The E31 crew breakup was negotiated from payroll and violence; they did NOT recruit that company. No default payroll boss hierarchy, territory/control or omniscient gang network.
Public gang reputation advances through witnesses and actual reports (including Sorell's pending ride and E31 survivors); cannot teleport news to Swain, TPP, Heisenberg, Darius or future enemies.
Use actual acquired goods and loot tension to change next objectives or personal choices; not a mandatory accounting scene or cash-count episode.
outlaw_operations.new_action: Within current doctrine make organized crime *functional*: a real chosen score, reconnaissance and competing incentives, different member risk/property priorities, real job leader agreement, specialist participation, negotiated loot/ownership when shown, practical hiding/exposure, concrete victory, personal fallout, adversary reporting. Not a rigid heist template; not all steps require narration.

Clifford: revenge and real humiliation/physical limitations, choices around TP tattoo and Arthur/Chris antagonism; no second Jack body.

tpp.repair: T.P.P. needs independent objectives, constraint-driven progression and occasional successful or failed crimes with their own consequences. Rival contact should emerge from overlapping actual targets, evidence, grudges, known ties or self-marketing, NOT a pre-scripted TPP cameo every episode or a miraculous travel/knowledge shortcut. The gang and TPP can both make money or both lose; neither always wins. Distinct TPP humor engines change scenes rather than shouting familiar catchphrases.
tpp.clock: Track last witnessed TPP HQ/rent/time and any actual new evidence. World time moves; do not invent late fees, dues paid, rival theft, work completed, distances, message receipt, secret gang locations or criminal success.

season3_roster.gaps: The active 90,349-character outline still has E29 state and 'next_new_main_episode'=30. Its Magneto status is stale after E30 and lacks E31 Katarina events and two chests. Actor-specific statuses must be overlaid with delivered manuscripts/checkpoints, not silently treated current or rewritten wholesale. S3 also contains numerous expanded Darkin, female champion and other cross-regional registers; this focused register list is NOT a full audit of every entry or matchup.
season3_roster.world_scene_policy: Every independent faction/character has own desire, real present access, actual knowledge, capacity and imperfect response timing. Major actors may act off camera only when supported by causal evidence; do not invent all their wins/damages just to prove they exist. A native faction's internal politics should cause consequences in reachable scenes and inform their reaction, not a headcount cameo.

editorial_roots: Recent episodes prioritize a contained transaction and close it, while roster, rivalry and factional consequence strands often fail to return organically.
An outline remembers *who exists* but poorly tracks who has acted, can hear what, wants what, and which pending clock is ripe.
Story feels like isolated set pieces rather than intersecting agency because intra-Sins relationship consequences and external rival operations are not paid off often enough.
Worldbuilding cannot be repaired by a mandatory crossover parade or offscreen invented news; use sourced access and advancing motives.

correction.procedure: Use existing Season3_Scene_Decision_Doctrine_20261010.md rather than new scene-building framework. Before draft, retrieve relevant COMPLETE owners; reconcile delivered branch; identify locally feasible intersections of Sins personal score, another faction's existing desire, one active interpersonal consequence, and plausible world knowledge/clock. Only choose people when actual causal access supports it.
correction.review: For final prose, document tangible passages where the gang's criminal model and member roles changed action, relationships evolved, external actors chose independently, TPP either developed a supported separate strand or remained absent for a clear reason, and Runeterra roster consequences matched correct delivered statuses. Absence isn't itself an error if scene grounds it; repeating it for episodes while rivalry never develops is.
do_not: No mass time skip, reset, new organization rank, new faction knowledge, Kaze absolute leadership, new gang property or territory, extra loot, automatic TPP membership before on-page event, reset of E31 Katarina, replay of inactive old Season3, 30-person cameo roll call, roster-completion quota or fabricated witness reports.
